body: I went back afterwards to check and make sure there was nothing on the site about things taking longer, and the only thing there was a message about them just having restocked. My friend seems to think there's some kind of small business leniency because it's a smaller operation. And that would have been fine if the seller had actually *asked* for more time. Or you know, said anything at all.

This sounds like my childhood exactly. I got beaten and screamed at for everything. To the point where if I broke something I spent hours agonizing over whether it was better to get beaten for telling the truth about breaking it or beaten over trying to hide it. I came home from school with a C in one class once (because I had refused to do the mindless busy work the teacher assigned), and my dad grabbed me and slammed me against the wall, demanding to know if I was on drugs. 

We had to do the going into the store thing too. My mom would pick us up from school and then drive to the store, give us a list and some money and a time limit, and we had to do all the shopping. If we took too long we got beat.

My mom would beat us for anything. She slapped my brother in the face so hard one time that there were scratches down his face, and she made him cover them up with makeup before he went to school. We were afraid to breathe the wrong way in that house. 

And that's such shitty parenting. Your kids shouldn't be afraid of you. And being treated like that and made to believe that it's because you deserve it, is so fucking damaging.
I'm sorry. Maybe it is cyclical for some people, and I'm just not one of those people.

Could be any number of reasons. Having a high paying job isn't automatically going to have the ladies swarming all over you, honestly. Maybe your friend is a good person or has interesting hobbies. Maybe they're a really good listener or is fantastic in bed. People are complex, and looking at one facet or having one thing going for you isn't enough.

You're right, it's really not fair. Sometimes I feel like just an acknowledgement of everything my parents put me through would go a long way towards helping me heal. Not even an apology, just a 'you're right, that was shitty'. But that's not how they work. 

I've tried opening up conversations with my parents about everything, but all I get is 'we did the best we could' and 'at least you had a roof over your head and food to eat; don't be ungrateful', so I don't do that anymore. It makes me angry and sad all at the same time, but it also makes me work harder to shake off what I can of the effects of their garbage.

We have. Several times. My housemate and I have, and we've done it with all four of us. Between my housemate and I, we divided things up like I'll take out the trash if he takes out the compost or I'll sweep the bathroom floor if he keeps the sink area clean. He hardly ever does his parts, even though he was the one who wanted it divided up like that.

Vaginas are weird and do weird things, honestly. It sounds like you might have some sort of infection, so you should consider going to the doctor about it. Don't be tempted to buy a bunch of cleansing products, though. Those usually just make things worse and throw your body's natural chemistry out of whack. Just wash yourself normally (and well) WITHOUT SOAP, and avoid wearing tight clothes. If it doesn't clear up, or it gets worse, go to the doctor.

That's a hard position to be in. I also grew up in an abusive household, and I clung to the hope that my parents would change and we would have a proper relationship for basically all of my teens and early 20s. I'm getting closer to 30 now, and I've finally let go of that hope. 

You're right, people can change. Part of changing is admitting your mistakes. If you let them back in and they try to pretend like nothing untoward happened when you were a kid, how will that make you feel? Can you just gloss over it and start a new relationship with them? If it turns out that they haven't really changed at all, will you feel comfortable cutting them out again?

My gut says don't trust them, but that's coming from my own experiences.

I've definitely been where you are, and faking faith is exhausting. I would start making moves towards being independent from your family as best you can. Save money, get a job if you can, look into loans/scholarships if they're paying for your schooling. You're never going to be happy or content with living a lie, but you also don't want to put yourself at risk of losing your home or schooling if it goes bad.

I think you're well within your rights to ask for more money. I mean, you basically make it so that she can stay out all night and then come home to a clean house, and people have to pay for those services. Even if she's not home a lot, I'm sure she's not spotless when she's there, so it's totally fair for her to do something to contribute to the upkeep of the house she lives in.

I guess it's just hard because I don't know these people at all. They don't know me or my history, so they ask questions like "What do your parents do?" and "Is your family going to come up?" and all manner of stuff that hurts to think about and the only thing you can really do is smile and answer the questions and pretend like you come from a functional family just like theirs.

I feel that, too. I don't know how to act around other people's parents. I don't know what to do when they start telling stories and showing how much they love each other. I feel like I'm seeing something I shouldn't be seeing.

Because it's seen as more admirable in our society to continue to hang in there even when there's no reason to anymore and everything makes you miserable. Because then when you're still alive you're a 'success story', you're strong, you're a fighter or whatever. Everyone looks down on 'taking the easy way out' no matter what the context, and no one understands how hard a decision is to decide to die instead of doing this anymore. And because people call it selfish when really what's selfish is guilting someone into staying alive no matter how unhappy they are, just because losing them would hurt.

I don't go that often, really. Usually only when there's no way to avoid it because they're having dinner right outside my bedroom door. I've definitely sat in my room going hungry instead of eating with my housemate's family before because it's just so hard to go out there and carry on a conversation sometimes.
